Positional encoding in the Transformer is a mechanism used to inject information about the relative or absolute position of tokens in a sequence into the model. This is necessary because the Transformer model contains no recurrence and no convolution, which means it cannot inherently capture the order of the sequence.

The positional encoding is added to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks. It has the same dimension as the embeddings, so the two can be summed. The Transformer uses sine and cosine functions of different frequencies to create the positional encoding:

_PE_ ( _pos,_ 2 _i_ ) = _sin_ ( _pos/_ 10000 [2] _[i/d]_ [model] )

_PE_ ( _pos,_ 2 _i_ +1) = _cos_ ( _pos/_ 10000 [2] _[i/d]_ [model] )

where _pos_ is the position and _i_ is the dimension.

The authors chose this function because it allows the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset _k_, _PEpos_ + _k_ can be represented as a linear function of _PEpos_ [Vaswani et al. 2017, pp.6].

generated_answer:
A pooling layer is a type of layer in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) that aims to gradually reduce the dimensionality of the representation, thereby reducing the number of parameters and the computational complexity of the model [O'Shea and Nash 2015, pp.8].

The pooling layer operates over each activation map in the input and scales its dimensionality using the "MAX" function, which is commonly referred to as max-pooling. In most CNNs, max-pooling layers with kernels of a dimensionality of 2 × 2 are applied with a stride of 2 along the spatial dimensions of the input, which scales the activation map down to 25% of the original size while maintaining the depth volume to its standard size [O'Shea and Nash 2015, pp.8].

The role of the pooling layer is to perform downsampling along the spatial dimensionality of the given input, further reducing the number of parameters within that activation [O'Shea and Nash 2015, pp.5]. This helps to reduce the complexity of the model and improve its performance.
